match_question_text: The value of equilibrium constant (Kc) for the reaction 2HF(s) ⇌ H2(g) + F2(g) is 10^-13 at 2000°C. Calculate the value of Kp for this reaction:

set.question_text: The value of equilibrium constant (Kc) for the reaction 2HF(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + F₂(g) is 10⁻¹³ at 2000 °C. Calculate the value of Kp for this reaction:
set.explanation_short: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. Two moles of gas give two moles of gas, so Δn = 0 and Kp = Kc = 10⁻¹³.
set.explanation_long: Kp and Kc are related by Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn, where Δn is moles of gaseous products minus moles of gaseous reactants. For 2HF ⇌ H₂ + F₂, Δn = (1 + 1) − 2 = 0, so (RT)⁰ = 1 and Kp = Kc = 10⁻¹³. (The paper prints HF as a solid, 2HF(s), which is impossible at 2000 °C and a misprint; the key treats HF as a gas, and the equation is shown that way here. Taking the misprint literally gives Δn = 2 and option D.)
set.explanation_trick: Equal moles of gas on both sides → Kp = Kc.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — there is no factor of 2 in Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — 186 × 10⁻¹³ is Kc × RT, which would need Δn = 1.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — 3.48 × 10⁻⁹ is Kc(RT)², which would need Δn = 2.

explanation_options.c: Also used as a shielding gas, but the key marks helium.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — krypton is too rare and costly; it is used in some lamps.

match_question_text: SPOT THE ERROR: We were ten miles up the highway (when I happened)[a] (to saw this)[b] (classified advertisement)[c] (in the newspaper.)[d]

set.question_text: SPOT THE ERROR: (We were)[a] ten miles (up the)[b] highway when I happened (to saw this)[c] classified advertisement (in the)[d] newspaper.
set.explanation_short: 'To saw' is wrong: after 'to' the base form is needed — 'happened to see this'.
set.explanation_long: 'Happened' is followed by a to-infinitive, and an infinitive uses the base form of the verb: 'I happened to see this classified advertisement'. 'Saw' is the past tense of 'see' and cannot follow 'to'. The other underlined parts are correct.
set.explanation_trick: to + base verb: to see, never to saw.

match_question_text: SPOT THE ERROR: “(All is well)[a] (what ends well)[b],” (said the father)[c] (when he had finished the story.)[d]

set.explanation_short: The proverb is 'All is well that ends well' — 'what' should be 'that'.
set.explanation_long: The fixed proverb reads 'All's well that ends well'. The relative pronoun referring back to 'all' is 'that', not 'what', so the underlined 'is well what' contains the error. The reporting clause and the rest of the sentence are correct.
set.explanation_trick: All … that: 'all that glitters', 'all's well that ends well'.

explanation_options.c: Wrong — 'when he had finished' is correct past perfect.

match_question_text: Which of the following is the correct sequence of PCR?
match_option_a: Heating → Cooling → Add Primer → Copying of strand

set.explanation_short: PCR: heat to separate the DNA strands, cool so the primers can attach, then DNA polymerase copies each strand.
set.explanation_long: Each PCR cycle starts by heating the DNA to about 94 °C so the two strands separate. The mixture is then cooled so that the short primers bind (anneal) to their complementary sites on the single strands, and finally DNA polymerase extends the primers, copying each strand. The textbook sequence is therefore heating → cooling with primers → copying. (In a laboratory the primers are already in the tube before heating, but they can only attach after the strands have been separated and cooled.)

explanation_options.a: Correct — heating, cooling, primer attachment, copying.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — primers attach only once the mixture has cooled.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — primers cannot attach before the strands are separated by heating.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — the cycle starts with heating, not cooling.

match_question_text: Which one of the following is the ultimate distributional unit within which a species is restrained by the limitations of its physical structure and physiology?

set.explanation_short: Grinnell defined the niche as the ultimate distributional unit within which a species is held by its structural and physiological limits.
set.explanation_long: The phrase in the question is Joseph Grinnell's classic definition of the ecological niche: the ultimate distributional unit within which each species is held by its structural and instinctive limitations. A habitat is simply the place where an organism lives; an ecosystem and a biome are much larger units that contain many species.

explanation_options.a: Correct — this is the definition of a niche.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — a biome is a large regional community.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — an ecosystem includes many species and their environment.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — a habitat is only the place where a species lives.

match_question_text: A gene that has more than one phenotypic effect is called

set.question_text: When a gene suppresses the effects of a gene at another locus, this is known as
set.explanation_short: A gene masking the effect of a non-allelic gene at another locus is epistasis.
set.explanation_long: In epistasis one gene masks or suppresses the phenotypic expression of a different gene at another locus. Co-dominance and complete dominance are relationships between alleles of the same gene, and a mutation is a change in the DNA. (The paper prints 'expresses the effects of a gene at another focus', a misprint for suppresses … locus.)
set.explanation_trick: Epistasis = between different genes; dominance = between alleles of one gene.

explanation_options.a: Correct — one gene masks another non-allelic gene.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — co-dominance is between two alleles of the same gene.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — complete dominance is between alleles of the same gene.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — a mutation is a change in DNA, not an interaction between genes.

match_question_text: A gene which masks the expression of another non-allelic gene is called

set.question_text: A gene which affects two or more unrelated characteristics is called
set.explanation_short: A single gene affecting two or more unrelated characters is pleiotropic.
set.explanation_long: Pleiotropy is when one gene influences several apparently unrelated traits; for example, the sickle-cell allele affects red cell shape, resistance to malaria and damage to many organs. An epistatic gene masks another gene; dominant describes an allele that hides its partner; a mutant gene is simply altered.
set.explanation_trick: Pleio = many: one gene, many effects.

explanation_options.a: Correct — one gene, several unrelated effects.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — an epistatic gene masks the effect of another gene.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — dominance is about one allele hiding another.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — mutant only means the gene is altered.
